title: Intelligence between things
description: An essay on distributed cognition, bioelectricity and memory, and a testable proposal for learning persistent relations and reasoning through sparse local activation.

title: Why World Models Need Memory
description: MAPA proposes a memory hierarchy for world-model prediction: an episodic buffer, consolidated landmarks, and gated adaptation. This essay develops the biological motivation, architectural proposal, failure modes, and experiments needed to test it.

title: Cheeger: Learning to Segment by Cutting Graphs
description: Cheeger builds a differentiable spectral segmentation head that learns graph affinities and the response applied to Laplacian eigenvectors. The article explains the mathematical foundations, implementation, experiments, and current limitations.

title: Engram: Building a Vector Memory Engine in Rust
description: Engram is a Redis-wire-compatible vector-memory engine written in Rust with libc as its only dependency. This article walks through its event loop, SIMD kernels, HNSW index, persistence, worker pool, benchmarks, and remaining limitations.

title: Divergent Thinking: Astrocytes, the Supervisors of the Tripartite Synapse
description: This essay examines research on astrocytic neuromodulation and the tripartite synapse, then connects it to associative memory and diffusion models. Its architectural interpretation is an argument developed from that research, rather than an experimentally validated AI system.

title: Understanding Principles of OOP Through Clash Royale
description: Clash Royale provides concrete examples for inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, abstraction, and composition. Java examples show how these ideas fit together and why the diamond problem matters.

title: A Quick Deep Dive into Energy Landscapes and Free Energy Models
description: Energy-based models score configurations and seek low-energy states, offering a different perspective from sequential token prediction. This essay explores attractors, denoising, memory, and the author’s view of reasoning as convergence.

title: How Spectral Graph Theory Connects to Advanced Memory Dynamics in the Human Brain
description: Graph Laplacians and diffusion provide a mathematical lens for studying relaxation and smoothing on networks. This essay connects that lens to memory dynamics, inhibition, and consolidation in the brain.

title: How to Walk Someone Through the MAPA Proposal
description: A narrative guide to explaining MAPA in an interview or panel, including the motivation, proposed mechanisms, mathematical questions, and failure modes. It distinguishes established foundations from hypotheses and planned validation.
